figures.caption: Figure 1: Five-layer smart renewable energy grid architecture with the proposed CNN-LSTM IDS deployed as a passive tap at the Layer 3/4 boundary.
Table 2: Threat model aligned with the five-category smart grid cyberthreat taxonomy of Ruan et al. [3].
Figure 7: Learning rate sensitivity analysis over η ∈ {10−4, . . . , 10−2}. Accuracy and F1-score both peak at η=0.001, confirming it as the optimal operating point.
Table 7: Efficiency comparison of all evaluated models. GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3080; CPU: Intel Core i7-12700K at batch size 100.
Figure 2: End-to-end workflow of the proposed CNN-LSTM IDS framework from data collection through preprocessing, training, and edge deployment.
Table 3: Layer-by-layer specification of the proposed Hybrid CNN-LSTM IDS (∼166K parameters; GPU: 2.3 ms/batch at batch 64; CPU: 8.2 ms/batch = 0.082 ms/sample at batch 100).
Table 4: Performance comparison of all six models on CICIDS2017 under 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Best results are highlighted in bold.

Figure 6: Training and validation loss of the proposed CNN-LSTM on CICIDS2017. Cross-entropy decreases from 1.45 to 0.06 over 51 epochs with a negligible train–validation gap, confirming no overfitting.

Figure 11: False-positive and false-negative rates per attack class on CICIDS2017. False negative rates exceed false positive rates across all classes, indicating residual errors are missed attacks rather than false alarms.

Figure 10: Precision-recall-F1 tradeoff versus classification threshold for the proposed CNN-LSTM. The optimal threshold τ∗≈0.48 maximizes F1-score and serves as the operational calibration reference.
Figure 4: Temporal flow-rate patterns for benign, DoS Hulk, and DoS Slowloris traffic, illustrating the need for both CNN spatial and LSTM temporal modeling.
Figure 5: Training and validation accuracy of the proposed CNN-LSTM on CICIDS2017. The model converges to 98.4% validation accuracy at epoch 51 with a consistently narrow train–validation gap.

Figure 12: Validation accuracy convergence of CNN, LSTM, and the proposed CNN-LSTM over 51 epochs on CICIDS2017. The hybrid model leads from epoch 1 and converges ∼5 epochs faster than standalone LSTM.
Figure 9: Multi-class Precision-Recall curves (one-vs-rest) on CICIDS2017. The CNN-LSTM achieves AP = 0.983, maintaining higher precision than all baselines particularly above recall = 0.6.
Figure 3: Proposed Hybrid CNN-LSTM IDS architecture with dual 1D-convolutional blocks, a reshape bridge, a 128-unit LSTM, and a multi-class softmax output.
Table 6: Cross-dataset generalization results. Models are trained and tested on the same dataset; rows show all combinations evaluated.

Figure 13: Ablation study showing the F1-score drop from removing each component. SMOTE balancing causes the largest single drop (−3.7 pp), confirming preprocessing quality as the dominant performance factor.
Table 1: Comparative summary of representative IDS approaches.
Table 5: Per-class performance of the proposed CNN-LSTM on CICIDS2017. SMOTE is applied to training only; Infiltration results (7 test instances) are reported for completeness.
Figure 8: ROC curves for all six models on CICIDS2017. The CNN-LSTM achieves AUC = 0.995, with the largest margin over baselines in the low-FPR region critical for operational deployment.
